thesis: Edgar mints a 1/1 Vampire from the command zone on every Vampire cast, the sacrifice outlets - six cost no mana - turn those bodies into death events, four death drains and four gain-to-loss converters (three read 'that much', Blight-Priest reads 'each opponent loses 1') bill the table on every one of them without a point of combat damage, and the game ends when a converter meets Bloodthirsty Conqueror - three verified two-card infinites, all through one card, or an attack through Bloodletter that drains fourteen a seat before blockers.

stages.label: THIRTY-FIVE LANDS, SEVEN ROCKS AND A COST REDUCER AIMED AT THE IGNITION EVENT
stages.what_it_does: Thirty-three land entries, thirty-five copies (Swamp x3), seven rocks, and Urza's Incubator, which takes up to {2} of GENERIC cost off every Vampire creature spell - the one mana card aimed at the ignition event rather than at mana in general. Generic only: over the 34 Vampire creature spells in cards.json (the commander and the Keeper's front face included) 19 get the full {2}, 7 get {1} and 8 get nothing, and the eight include most of the cheap casts - Tithe Drinker, Cordial, Cruel Celebrant, Bloodghast. Its biggest single discount is Edgar himself, {3}{R}{W}{B} to {1}{R}{W}{B}. The declared ramp component (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, the three Talismans, the Incubator) is drawn in 75.8% of games, mean turn 3.43, 59.9% by turn six. deck-audit reads ramp AT (10 copies against 10-12, counting Ashnod's Altar and Master of Dark Rites, both filed elsewhere here), mana-base UNDER by one (35 against 36-38), mana-sources AT the Burgess 40, and colour-sources AT in every colour (B 37 of 36, R 22 of 22, W 24 of 22). Two lands do a second job and stay here because mana is the louder one: Midgar's Adventure half sacrifices a creature to draw two, Takenuma's channel returns a creature card to hand. Phyrexian Tower is NOT here: its '{T}, Sacrifice a creature: Add {B}{B}' is the declaration's fifth free outlet and it is filed under conversion. Master of Dark Rites is filed under ignition: its mana costs a body ('{T}, Sacrifice another creature: Add {B}{B}{B}') and deck-facts flags it as spend-only on Vampire, Cleric and Demon SPELLS - in this 99 every such spell is a Vampire, enumerated over type lines in cards.json - including the two triple-black costs, Bloodletter of Aclazotz and Vein Ripper. Exotic Orchard is the pilot's red fix; the goldfish cannot rank one land against another.

stages.label: A VAMPIRE SPELL IS CAST, AND A BODY APPEARS FROM THE COMMAND ZONE
stages.what_it_does: Nothing in this deck starts until a Vampire spell is CAST: Edgar's eminence makes a 1/1 Vampire from the command zone on every other Vampire cast, so the half the pilot owns is free, undrawable and out of removal's reach, and the half that has to be found is the spell. The declared castable-Vampire leg is eight cards, drawn in 84.9% of games (45.6% of opening sevens, mean turn 3.09, 70.3% by turn six) - the healthiest figure in the brief; only two of the eight sit here, because the other six do a louder second job: Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant and Vraan drain on death (output), Bloodghast and Charismatic Conqueror make bodies (fodder), Cordial Vampire turns deaths into size (conversion). Tithe Drinker and Master of Dark Rites are the two whose contribution is dominated by being the cast: a {W}{B} lifelinker whose extort pays {W/B} per spell for a one-point drain, and a {B} body whose '{T}, Sacrifice another creature: Add {B}{B}{B}' turns a token into the next Vampire, Cleric or Demon spell - mana that costs a body (roles: sac-outlet, ramp:dork), the sixth no-mana outlet, which the declared free-outlet group does not name. Enumerated from cards.json type lines, the 99 holds eleven Vampire creature spells at mana value two or less and the declared leg omits three of them (Viscera Seer, Bloodtithe Harvester, Edgar, Ancient Bloodlord) - see proposed_goldfish_edits. The commander is cast by turn six in 69.8% of goldfish games (mean 5.78, median 6) and the three verified loops do not need him on the battlefield; stack 003 has him attacking as the seventh Vampire, and that board's seat at 14 needed all seven triggers - a body count, not a requirement for Edgar in particular.

stages.label: DRAW WHEN THINGS DIE, AND FOUR TUTORS THAT ARE THE ASSISTED COLUMN
stages.what_it_does: The pilot's required axis: every logged game ran dry by turn eight to ten. The declared draw component is seven cards, drawn in 75.2% of games (mean turn 2.90, 63.6% by turn six). Four of the ten draw cards here read a DEATH - Morbid Opportunist (once a turn), Liliana (every creature of yours), Erebos (pay 2 life per death), Crossway Troublemakers (pay 2 life per Vampire death) - and Clavileno's is a death the deck arranges: the attacking Vampire it names draws a card and leaves a tapped 4/3 flier when it dies. Two read an ENTRY, which is the ignition event itself: Welcoming Vampire and Caretaker's Talent draw once a turn when a small creature or a token enters, so every eminence mint is a card. Phyrexian Arena and Twilight Prophet are upkeep draw. The goldfish prices this as a floor: of 16 cards that draw, 8 are modelled, death-draw counts only on deaths the model produces, and mean extra cards is 3.12 by turn ten; deck-audit reads card-advantage UNDER (7 against 10) and names Clavileno, Anje, Bloodtithe Harvester, Castle Locthwain, Minas Tirith and Midgar as uncounted. The four tutors are fuel of a different kind - the 'assisted' column: the infinite assembles in 22.1% of games unassisted and 57.3% with a tutor, 10.8% against 33.3% by turn six. Diabolic Intent is also a death: its additional cost sacrifices a creature, which fires every output on the way to the card. Erebos is a sacrifice outlet and a -2/-1 as well; it files here because the draw clause is the static one.

stages.label: THE BODIES, AND THE TWO CARDS THAT DOUBLE THEM
stages.what_it_does: What the outlets eat is 1/1 Vampire tokens, and this stage is what makes more of them than eminence alone. Two replacement doublers - Anointed Procession and Elspeth, Storm Slayer - apply to every token event in the deck: eminence, Charismatic Conqueror's lifelink Vampires (one per untapped artifact or creature an opponent declines to tap), Bloodline Keeper's 2/2 fliers, Preacher's and Clavileno's tokens, Elenda's death payout. The declared multiplier component is thin: two cards, 13.7% of opening sevens, drawn in 37.1% of games (mean turn 4.38, 25.3% by turn six; 74.3% assisted). The stacks that priced the doubling (002: 1->2->4; 010: 1->2->4->8 under all six orders) passed the checker on boards that cast Gifted Aetherborn under Mondrak, Glory Dominus, and both cards left the 99 - so on v2.1.0 the token math is a claim awaiting a current board, and it is the first open question. Bloodghast is fodder of another kind: it returns from the graveyard on every land drop, so it is a body the outlets can eat every turn - and the goldfish reads only the cast body: goldfish_turn.py's one landfall read is the Treasure channel and no channel returns a card from the graveyard, so model-coverage lists Bloodghast as seen for the 2/1 and nothing for the return. Olivia, Crimson Bride returns a creature card tapped and attacking on each attack; she files here because what she produces is a body back, on a condition the deck sets (control a legendary Vampire or it is exiled). Eminence tokens do not re-trigger eminence - they are created, not cast - and no doubler touches a Vampire SPELL.

stages.label: SEVEN OUTLETS, AND THE TWO THAT MAKE A DEATH PAY IN SIZE
stages.what_it_does: The engine proper: a body goes in, a death event comes out, and every output and every death-draw reads that event. Six outlets cost no mana; the DECLARED free-outlet group is five of them, drawn in 69.1% of games (mean turn 3.55, 53.3% by turn six): Ashnod's Altar ({C}{C} back), Phyrexian Tower ({B}{B} back), Viscera Seer (scry 1), Vish Kal (X counters, X the sacrificed power, and the counters come off as -1/-1 to a creature - the pilot's answer to indestructible) and Yahenni (indestructible until end of turn). The sixth, Master of Dark Rites ({T}, sacrifice another creature, for {B}{B}{B}), is filed under ignition and is not in the declared group (proposed edit). Two cost {2}: Edgar, Ancient Bloodlord (a counter and menace, plus 1 life on every other death - a life GAIN, which is a converter trigger) and Anje (each opponent loses 2, you gain 2, from a creature or a Blood token). Erebos and Diabolic Intent are outlets too, filed under fuel. The goldfish converts at 1.41 sacrifices by turn ten and models table deaths at 0.858 of your creatures a turn (a V3 Forge rate), so the conversion count is the model's policy. Cordial Vampire and Elenda are the two cards that make a death pay in SIZE rather than in a trigger: Cordial puts a counter on every Vampire per death; Elenda takes one per other death and leaves X lifelink tokens when she dies - created, so the doublers apply. No presentable stack names an outlet. Forge's AI activates the outlets whose payoff its evaluator prices and not the ones that make mana: on the 2026-10-01 V3 run (200 games) Viscera Seer 44 activations in 122 battlefield turns, Vish Kal 336, Yahenni 7 - Ashnod's Altar 0 in 121, Master of Dark Rites 0 in 137 (engine_casts), so a Forge figure is a floor on the mana-making half of this stage.

stages.label: LIFE LOSS WITHOUT COMBAT: DEATH DRAINS, GAIN CONVERTERS, AND THE DENIAL FOUR
stages.what_it_does: Three kinds of output, none of them combat damage. (1) Drains that read a DEATH: the declared four - Blood Artist (target player, 1), Cruel Celebrant (each opponent, 1, your creatures only), Vraan (each opponent, 2, once a turn, your creatures only), Vein Ripper (target opponent, 2, ANY creature's death, and ward - sacrifice a creature) - are drawn in 60.4% of games (mean turn 3.88, 44.1% by turn six). Beside them Sanctum Seeker drains per attacking Vampire, Wispdrinker per small creature entering (every eminence token), Ingris pings per attacker. (2) Converters that turn GAIN into loss: Vito, Sanguine Bond and Enduring Tenacity read 'whenever you gain life, target opponent loses that much life' word for word; Marauding Blight-Priest reads 'each opponent loses 1'. Every drain in (1) but Ingris gains you life (Ingris deals damage and gains nothing), so every death is also a converter trigger - and with a loss-to-gain half from wincon on the battlefield the converter IS the loop; that pairing is the fact tier (004, 006, 012). (3) Removal and denial: Path, Anguished Unmaking (the one answer to a noncreature permanent, 20.3% drawn, 66.6% assisted), Olivia's Wrath (-X/-X to every non-Vampire), Anowon's upkeep edict, Drana and Linvala's lock on activated abilities, Captivating Vampire's steal, Olivia Voldaren's ping and steal, Bloodtithe Harvester's -X/-X. deck-audit: interaction AT 8, breadth UNDER with no graveyard or land answer. The goldfish prices the drains as a floor - 6.32 cumulative by turn ten, 69.4% of games draining - with Sanctum Seeker, Anje and Twilight Prophet not modelled.

stages.label: FOUR HELD, THREE OF THEM FREE OR DOUBLED WITH EDGAR OUT
stages.what_it_does: Held, not cast. Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver are free 'if you control a commander' - Edgar on the battlefield, which the goldfish has by turn six in 69.8% of games - and Akroma's Will is both modes under the same condition. The component is drawn in 60.6% of games (mean turn 3.84, 45.1% by turn six) and deck-audit reads protection AT 7, counting Erebos, Vein Ripper and Yahenni, bodies that protect only themselves and are filed elsewhere. What each one reaches matters for the loop, because its halves are of different types: Flawless Maneuver and Akroma's Will name CREATURES, so they cover Conqueror, Vito and Tenacity-as-creature but never Exquisite Blood or Sanguine Bond; Teferi's Protection phases out every permanent and is the only one of the four that answers a SWEEPER that exiles, bounces or gives -X/-X; Deflecting Swat retargets one targeted spell or ability of any kind, exile included. Stack 012 settles one piece's own insurance: destroy or -X/-X on Enduring Tenacity returns it as an enchantment with the drain ability intact and the loop does not pause - only exile, bounce, a graveyard replacement, a countered return trigger or enchantment removal after the return breaks that half. This is the one stage the map agrees with completely: all four sit together in city-0's Insurance hood, because protection is what the card SAYS.

stages.label: THE LOSS-TO-GAIN HALF, AND THE DOUBLER
stages.what_it_does: The game ends when a loss-to-gain half meets a gain-to-loss converter from output, and the thin half is this one: Bloodthirsty Conqueror and Exquisite Blood are 13.7% of opening sevens against the converters' 25.8%, and the whole infinite assembles in 22.1% of games (57.3% with a tutor), 10.8% by turn six (33.3% assisted), mean turn 5.98. Three loops are on the fact tier and all three run through Conqueror - with Vito (004), with Sanguine Bond (006), with Enduring Tenacity (012) - each deterministic, shortcut-legal, zero mana, a full table kill from any life-gain seed, and unbroken by an opponent dying mid-loop. That is why Conqueror is the single point of failure of the VERIFIED wincon rather than of the deck: Exquisite Blood's loops with Vito (001) and Sanguine Bond (005) also passed the checker but are withheld, because their seed creature was Vampire Nighthawk and it left the 99; the loop text is unchanged and a current-board re-run is the second open question. deck-facts counts eight contained two-card infinites; Blight-Priest's two are candidates. The second route is Bloodletter: 'if an opponent would lose life during your turn, they lose twice that much' doubles every output on your turn, and stack 003 is the proof - seven attacking Vampires, Sanctum Seeker draining 14 per seat before blockers, Edgar one of the seven. Its declared component is Bloodletter plus Sanctum Seeker alone, 4.5% assembled (33.0% assisted, mean turn 6.46), and that second leg is too narrow: every death drain the outlets fire on your turn is doubled too (proposed edit). Bloodletter and Anguished Unmaking are deck-audit's two priced single points of failure, 7.1% of opening sevens each.

map_disagreements.component: THE SURVIVING INFINITE (the loop's two halves)
map_disagreements.why: The map clusters on what a card says, and the loop is a relation between two sentences printed on different kinds of card: Conqueror reads as a 5/5 flying deathtouch body with a lifegain clause (Payoffs), Vito as a legendary body with an activated ability (Bodies), Exquisite Blood, Sanguine Bond, Tenacity and Blight-Priest as drain text (Finishers). No single city holds a complete loop, which is exactly why the verified lines are the only fact-tier evidence that the halves belong together; Spellbook's eight contained lines are candidates.

An outlet is defined by a cost - 'Sacrifice a creature:' - that is a few words on a land (Phyrexian Tower), an artifact that also reads as a rock (Ashnod's Altar), a one-drop Vampire (Viscera Seer) and two legendary bodies (Vish Kal, Yahenni). The embedding reads the type line and the rest of the text and files each where those point; the job they share is invisible to it. The conversion stage spans five cities, the most of any stage.

map_disagreements.component: A castable Vampire drawn (the ignition leg)
map_disagreements.why: Ignition is a property of the type line and the mana value - 'Vampire', two or less - and the map reads through the ability text instead, so the eight declared casts sort by what they do after they resolve. The engine's first event has no city.

Death-draw (Morbid Opportunist) files with the death drains in Finishers, entry-draw (Welcoming Vampire) with the entry payoffs in Payoffs, the planeswalker and the Class with the big bodies. The map sorts draw by its trigger event, which is a correct reading of the text and the wrong reading of the stage.

Full agreement, recorded as the control case: the four instants say what they do and nothing else, and the map puts them in one hood. Where the map and the engine agree it is because the card's text IS its job.

open_questions.question: On a v2.1.0 board - Edgar in the command zone, Anointed Procession and Elspeth, Storm Slayer on the battlefield - cast Tithe Drinker: how many 1/1 Vampire tokens does the single eminence trigger create, and does Elspeth's replacement apply to a trigger resolving from the command zone? (The 002/010 shape, re-run on cards still in the 99.)
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every figure about the fodder stage rests on stacks 002 and 010, which are withheld because Gifted Aetherborn and Mondrak left the list. Until a current board passes, the token engine the deck is named for has no fact-tier proof.

open_questions.question: Exquisite Blood + Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose and Exquisite Blood + Sanguine Bond on a current board, seeded by a Blood Artist trigger or Tithe Drinker's lifelink: deterministic, shortcut-legal and a table kill on the same terms as 004/006?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stacks 001 and 005 passed and are withheld only because their seed creature (Vampire Nighthawk) was cut. Until re-run, Bloodthirsty Conqueror is the wincon's single point of failure on the evidence; with them, the loss-to-gain half has verified redundancy.

open_questions.question: Marauding Blight-Priest + Bloodthirsty Conqueror with three opponents: Blight-Priest's 'each opponent loses 1 life' makes three separate loss events per gain, so Conqueror triggers three times and you gain 3 - does that loop kill the table, is it shortcut-legal, and what happens when one opponent leaves mid-loop?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The declaration counts Blight-Priest as a gain-to-loss half of THE SURVIVING INFINITE and nothing has verified it; its shape differs from the three verified loops. The answer decides whether the converter leg is four cards or three.

open_questions.question: Wispdrinker Vampire with a doubled eminence event (two 1/1 tokens entering at once): does 'whenever another creature you control with power 2 or less enters' trigger once per token, and does Welcoming Vampire's once-per-turn clause fire on the same event?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Wispdrinker is the one drain that bills on the ignition event rather than on a death, and stack 011 (withheld) found Mirkwood Bats fires once per token on a different clause. The count prices what a single Vampire cast is worth before anything dies.

open_questions.question: For a two-piece loop whose halves are a creature and an enchantment, under instant-speed removal at a bracket-4 table: which half to land first, and whether to hold protection or a tutor for the second - what does the strategy corpus say about sequencing and protecting a two-card combo?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stack 012 shows the halves differ in fragility (Tenacity survives destroy, Conqueror does not) and the protection stage reaches creatures and enchantments differently. The pilot asked for protection once the pieces are out; the sequencing rule is the coaching that follows from the model.

open_questions.question: How much does the free-outlet conversion count (1.41 sacrifices by turn ten) move if a body returns on every land drop - Bloodghast's landfall recursion, which the model does not see?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Bloodghast was added as recurring sacrifice fuel and reads as a one-shot 2/1 to the goldfish: goldfish_turn.py reads landfall only as a Treasure trigger and no channel returns a card from the graveyard (model-coverage: seen, for the body). The answer needs the recursion modelled first; until then every conversion figure on v2.1.0 is a floor by a known amount of unknown size.

previous_round.summary: Read against the 13:06 hand-off. The four cited stacks (003, 004, 006, 012) support every solid line and every stack-evidence note; every goldfish rate, audit axis and opening-seven figure re-derives exactly; the withheld-stack reasons check out. The model fails on one dashed line written as fact that is false for its own via card (lines[11]: Urza's Incubator cannot reduce Tithe Drinker's {W}{B}), one card fact omitted in a way that changes a count (Master of Dark Rites' ability costs '{T}, Sacrifice another creature' - a sixth no-mana outlet the 'five outlets are free' count misses), three role-membership evidence notes that miscount against engine-facts roles, and one superlative that fails enumeration (Ingris gains no life).

findings.claim: The Incubator takes {2} off every Vampire creature spell: a two-mana Vampire costs its coloured pips alone, so two casts a turn - two eminence events - become ordinary
findings.note: cards.json: Urza's Incubator reads 'Creature spells of the chosen type cost {2} less to cast'; a cost reduction lowers generic mana only, and Tithe Drinker - this line's own via card - costs {W}{B} with no generic, so the Incubator takes nothing off it. Enumerated over the eleven Vampire creature spells at MV<=2 in cards.json, the Incubator reduces exactly three (Blood Artist {1}{B}, Charismatic Conqueror {1}{W}, Vraan {1}{B}, each by one) and leaves eight untouched (Bloodghast, Bloodtithe Harvester, Cordial, Cruel Celebrant, Edgar AB, Master of Dark Rites, Tithe Drinker, Viscera Seer). The 'two casts a turn become ordinary' consequence is asserted as fact on a dashed line. Re-via the line to a card the reducer touches (or to a 3+ drop such as Bloodletter {1}{B}{B}{B} -> {B}{B}{B}) and state the generic-only limit. Mechanically checkable: a mana->ignition line via a ramp:cost-reduction card must have a second via whose mana_cost contains a generic component.

findings.claim: Urza's Incubator, which takes {2} off every Vampire creature spell
findings.note: Same artifact: the reduction is up to {2} of GENERIC cost. Of the 24 Vampire creature spells in cards.json the full {2} comes off only those with two or more generic pips; eight of the eleven cheap Vampires get nothing and Bloodletter gets {1}. 'the one mana card aimed at the ignition event' is fine; 'takes {2} off every' is not.

findings.claim: a {B} body whose {B}{B}{B} pays only for the next Vampire, Cleric or Demon spell
findings.note: cards.json: Master of Dark Rites reads '{T}, Sacrifice another creature: Add {B}{B}{B}. Spend this mana only to cast Vampire, Cleric, and/or Demon spells.' The mana is not free - it costs a body - and engine-facts roles tag the card sac-outlet (and sac-cost). The stage describes it as a ramp dork and omits the sacrifice cost entirely, so the model's filing argument ('dominated by being the cast') rests on half the card. It is the deck's sixth no-mana sacrifice outlet (tap-cost, like Phyrexian Tower) and the only one that turns a token into three black mana for the next Vampire cast - a fodder->conversion->ignition loop the model never draws.

findings.claim: Five outlets are free - no mana, no tap except the Tower's
findings.note: Enumerated over every 'Sacrifice ... creature' cost in cards.json: Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Tower ({T}), Viscera Seer, Vish Kal, Yahenni, Master of Dark Rites ({T}) cost no mana - six, not five. The DECLARED free-outlet component is five (goldfish_targets), and the 69.1% / 3.55 / 53.3% figures are that group's; the sentence conflates the declared group with the deck. Say 'the declared five' and name the sixth. The thesis's 'seven outlets' inherits the same undercount (seven is 5 free + Edgar AB + Anje by this filing; Master, Erebos and Diabolic Intent make ten by oracle text).

findings.note: engine-facts roles: sac-outlet = Anje, Ashnod's Altar, Edgar AB, Erebos, Master of Dark Rites, Viscera Seer, Vish Kal, Yahenni.
